defect.message: The plain laminated elastomeric bearings are described only by type ("plain laminated elastomeric bearings, one under each girder end; four internal rubber layers 8 mm thick"). The bearing plan dimensions a and b (plan length/width, or the standard bearing model designation) are not given. These are required inputs: the shape factor is S = a·b/(2·t1·(a+b)) (JTG 3362-2018 8.7), the vertical stiffness Kv = count·a·b/(te·(1/Ee + 1/Eb))·1000 with Ee = 5.4·Ge·S² and the shear stiffness Kh = count·Ge·a·b/te·1000. The number of layers (4) and the layer thickness (8 mm) determine only te and t1, so a and b cannot be derived from the statements given, and the support springs cannot be computed. The description must also supply the elastomer shear modulus Ge if a non-standard value is intended; otherwise the standard Ge is assumed.

The span arrangement states "One continuous unit of three spans, 25 + 30 + 30 + 25 m (centre-to-centre of bearings)", i.e. it declares three spans but gives four bearing-centreline span lengths. The boundary description names "Abutment 0, Pier 1, Pier 2 and Abutment 3", which corresponds to four support lines and hence three spans, matching "three spans" but not the four listed lengths. It is therefore impossible to determine the actual span lengths (three of which would have to be chosen/omitted) and the number of spans/supports, so the model cannot be built as given.

The bridge's main girders are outside the scope of the knowledge graph. The description states "Steel plate girders acting compositely with a 0.25 m cast-in-place deck slab, 3 per span; steel girder depth 1.4 m, top flange 400 mm x 25 mm, bottom flange 500 mm x 30 mm, web 1345 mm x 16 mm, steel Q345". The knowledge graph only defines girder section types "small_box", "t_girder" and "cast_box", which are all concrete sections; compute_section_properties accepts only these three section types and cannot integrate a steel plate/composite section. There are no rules or clauses for steel members or steel grades (keyword searches "steel plate girder", "Q345", "flange", "composite" return no matches), and the material density rule JTGD60-4.2.1 applies only when material == 'prestressed_concrete'. Since the girder type (steel, composite) is not covered by the graph's rules and clauses, the bridge cannot be modeled as given; no values are invented.

The plain laminated elastomeric bearings are described only by their internal rubber layers ("four internal rubber layers 8 mm thick"). The bearing plan dimensions a and b (mm) are not given. The KG instance constraint C-02 requires complete bearing parameters for laminated elastomeric bearings (plane dimensions AND rubber layers: "板式橡胶支座需平面尺寸与橡胶层"), and the shape factor S = a*b/(2*t1*(a+b)) per JTG 3362-2018 8.7 needs a and b to compute the bearing stiffness. No default plan size is provided by the KG, so the bearing stiffness (S, Kv, Kh) and thus the boundary conditions cannot be determined without these dimensions.

The span arrangement is self-contradictory: the description states "[Span arrangement] One continuous unit of three spans, 25 + 30 + 30 + 25 m (centre-to-centre of bearings)", i.e. it declares three spans but gives four span lengths (25, 30, 30, 25 m). This conflicts with the boundary description, which lists exactly four support lines (Abutment 0, Pier 1, Pier 2, Abutment 3) and therefore only three spans between supports. It is impossible to determine which three of the four given values (25+30+30+25) are the real bearing-centre-line spans, so the span set to model cannot be established.

The girder is described as "Steel plate girders acting compositely with a 0.25 m cast-in-place deck slab, ... steel Q345", i.e. a composite steel-plate-girder section. The knowledge graph only covers concrete girders: the section-geometry schema offers only small_box / t_girder / cast_box, the modeling rule MR-02 computes A and I from a concrete cross-section ("外轮廓减内孔"), and the material rules (e.g. JTG3362-3.1.5, EC_TABLE) apply only to concrete grades. There is no rule, clause, section type or material model for steel plate girders or for a composite steel-girder/concrete-deck section, so the girder cannot be modelled within the scope of the KG.

The span arrangement contradicts itself: the description states "One continuous unit of three spans, 25 + 30 + 30 + 25 m (centre-to-centre of bearings)", which lists FOUR span lengths (25, 30, 30, 25 m) for what is declared to be THREE spans. The support lines given are "Abutment 0, Pier 1 and Abutment 3 ... Pier 2", i.e. four support lines (indices 0, 1, 2, 3), which define only three spans. Three spans require exactly three span lengths, and four span lengths require five support lines; the description supplies four of each, so the span counts and support indices cannot be reconciled. The model cannot be built as given without guessing whether a span length or a support line is missing/extra.

The description specifies laminated elastomeric bearings only by their rubber layer thickness and count ("plain laminated elastomeric bearings, one under each girder end; four internal rubber layers 8 mm thick") but gives no bearing plan dimensions (length a and width b). The governing rules JTG3362-8.7-S, JTG3362-8.7-Kv and JTG3362-8.7-Kh require a and b to compute the shape factor S = a*b/(2*t1*(a+b)) and hence the vertical and shear stiffnesses (Kv, Kh); the instance schema correspondingly expects a_mm and b_mm, and the knowledge graph supplies no default or standard bearing plan size. Without a and b the support spring stiffnesses cannot be determined, so the model cannot be built as given.

The description specifies "Steel plate girders acting compositely with a 0.25 m cast-in-place deck slab, 3 per span; steel girder depth 1.4 m, top flange 400 mm x 25 mm, bottom flange 500 mm x 30 mm, web 1345 mm x 16 mm, steel Q345". The knowledge graph's girder rules and section-integration schemas cover only concrete girder types (small_box, t_girder, cast_box) with material 'prestressed_concrete' — MR-02 computes A/I by integrating a concrete outer profile minus voids, and no rule, clause or section type covers a steel plate girder, structural steel Q345 material properties, or a steel-concrete composite section. This component therefore lies outside the scope of the knowledge graph and cannot be modeled as given.

The bearing description is incomplete: it states only "plain laminated elastomeric bearings, one under each girder end; four internal rubber layers 8 mm thick" but gives no plan dimensions. The KG constraint C-02 requires each laminated elastomeric bearing to have both plan dimensions, and clauses JTG3362-8.7-S, -Kv and -Kh compute the shape factor S and the vertical/shear stiffnesses from a * b (S = a*b/(2*t1*(a+b)); Kv and Kh scale with a*b). With a_mm and b_mm missing and no default supplied by the knowledge graph, the bearing stiffnesses cannot be determined and the model cannot be built.

The span arrangement is self-contradictory: the text states "One continuous unit of three spans, 25 + 30 + 30 + 25 m (centre-to-centre of bearings)", which gives four span lengths (25, 30, 30, 25) but claims three spans. Correspondingly, the bearings are described for only four support lines (Abutment 0, Pier 1, Pier 2, Abutment 3), which yields three spans, not four. Four span lengths (25+30+30+25) require five support lines, but no fifth support is given. The span count ("three"), the number of span lengths (four), and the number of described supports (four) cannot be reconciled.

The description specifies "Steel plate girders acting compositely with a 0.25 m cast-in-place deck slab ... steel girder depth 1.4 m, top flange 400 mm x 25 mm, bottom flange 500 mm x 30 mm, web 1345 mm x 16 mm, steel Q345". The knowledge graph covers only concrete girder types (small_box, t_girder, cast_box) and concrete girder rules: its section schemas have no steel plate-girder fields, girder.A/girder.I rules (MR-02) assume concrete section integration, and girder.Ec (JTG3362-3.1.5) draws from a concrete grade table. Queries for "steel", "steel plate girder" and "plate" return no matching rules or clauses. A steel plate girder with a composite concrete deck therefore lies outside the scope of the knowledge graph and cannot be modeled with its rules and clauses.

The plain laminated elastomeric bearings are specified only by their layering ("four internal rubber layers 8 mm thick"). Their plan dimensions are never given. The bearing shape factor S = a*b/(2*t1*(a+b)) (JTG 3362-2018 8.7) and consequently the vertical stiffness Kv = count*a*b/(te*(1/Ee+1/Eb))*1000 and shear stiffness Kh = count*Ge*a*b/te*1000 require the bearing plan length a and width b, which the description omits. No default plan size is provided by the knowledge graph, so support.0.S/.Kv/.Kh and support.1.S/.Kv/.Kh cannot be evaluated.

The bridge uses "Steel plate girders acting compositely with a 0.25 m cast-in-place deck slab ... steel girder depth 1.4 m, top flange 400 mm x 25 mm, bottom flange 500 mm x 30 mm, web 1345 mm x 16 mm, steel Q345". The knowledge graph covers only concrete girder types (small_box, t_girder, cast_box) with concrete section schemas, and its material rules are limited to concrete grades (JTG 3362-2018 Table 3.1.5 for Ec). There are no rules, clauses or section types for steel plate girders, steel-composite sections, or steel grade Q345, so no girder.single.A/I, girder.A/I, girder.Ec or girder.gamma decision can be derived. The component lies outside the scope of the knowledge graph.

defect.message: The span arrangement is internally inconsistent: it states "One continuous unit of three spans" but then gives four span lengths "25 + 30 + 30 + 25 m". A three-span unit implies 4 support lines (which matches the described bearings: Abutment 0, Pier 1, Pier 2, Abutment 3), but four spans imply 5 support lines, only 4 of which are described. The number of spans (three vs four) and hence the support/bearing layout cannot be determined without guessing.

The description does not give the plan dimensions (a_mm, b_mm) of the plain laminated elastomeric bearings. It states only "four internal rubber layers 8 mm thick", i.e. t1_mm and n_layers. The KG constraint C-02 requires each laminated elastomeric bearing to have complete parameters including plan dimensions, the shape factor rule JTG 3362-2018 clause 8.7 (S = a*b / (2*t1*(a+b))) needs a and b, and there is no rule or default in the knowledge graph that supplies them. Without a and b the bearing shape factor and the bearing shear/vertical stiffnesses (support.<k>.S / .Kv / .Kh) cannot be computed.

The span arrangement is internally contradictory and cannot be modeled as given. The description says "One continuous unit of three spans, 25 + 30 + 30 + 25 m (centre-to-centre of bearings)", but a three-span continuous unit has four support lines (three spans = three span lengths), and the supports are indeed enumerated as exactly four lines: "Abutment 0, Pier 1 ... Pier 2 ... Abutment 3". However, the span-length list gives FOUR values (25 + 30 + 30 + 25 m), which would require five support lines (four spans). The number of spans/bearings stated (three spans, supports 0-3) is thus inconsistent with the four span lengths listed, and it is impossible to determine which three lengths apply to the three spans without guessing.

The bridge uses steel plate girders ("Steel plate girders acting compositely with a 0.25 m cast-in-place deck slab... steel girder depth 1.4 m, top flange 400 mm x 25 mm, bottom flange 500 mm x 30 mm, web 1345 mm x 16 mm, steel Q345"). The knowledge graph covers only concrete girder types — its section schemas are small_box, t_girder and cast_box (all prestressed/precast concrete), the section-property rule MR-02 refers to concrete sections with wet joints and diaphragms, and the governing modulus clause JTG3362-3.1.5 is the concrete elastic-modulus table (grade in EC_TABLE). No rule, clause or section geometry exists for a steel plate girder or for a steel-concrete composite section, so the main-girder A, I and Ec cannot be modeled as given. This component falls outside the scope of the knowledge graph.
